subject: Throughput pinning request — BlackWeek seasonal spike (GreenCrest)
messages:
From: Lena Morales <lena.morales@greencrest.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@greencrest.com
Date: 2028-11-05T08:12:00Z
Subject: Throughput spike & temporary pinning request for BlackWeek

Hi Evelyn —

We’re ramping up for BlackWeek (Nov 20–27) and our traffic forecast shows a sustained 6x increase in prompt volume during peak hours. We’re on a Dedicated pool with Redwood (deal GC-2028-BLKWK) and had a couple of questions around short-term protections:

- Can Redwood provision a temporary throughput pin (guaranteed tokens/sec) for the 8–48 hour daily peak windows?
- How does Redwood’s queueing/preemption behave during multi-tenant maintenance or background rebalancing? We can’t risk tail latency spikes that will impact SLAs to our merchants.

We’re open to a one-week addendum to our Dedicated terms or an operations runbook that prevents preemption during the BlackWeek window. Attaching our traffic forecast for the week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Lena Morales
Head of Platform Ops, GreenCrest Logistics
Lena.morales@greencrest.com
+1 415 555 0123

Attachment: greencrest_traffic_forecast.csv (CSV, 42 KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Lena Morales <lena.morales@greencrest.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-05T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Throughput spike & temporary pinning request for BlackWeek

Lena —

Thanks for the heads up and for the forecast. We can absolutely discuss options to reduce risk during your peak window. Quick summary of what we can offer and what I need from you: 

1) Options we can consider (short term):
   - Temporary throughput pin: we can carve a soft-guarantee (reserved tokens/sec) for configured daily windows. This is implemented as a short-lived override on your Dedicated pool.
   - Maintenance blackout: schedule a maintenance blackout for the BlackWeek dates to avoid background preemption/rebalancing during your configured windows.
   - Priority lane + soft-reserve tokens: route your traffic through a priority queue that gets burst credits; helps with tail behavior while keeping overall utilization efficient.

2) What we need from GreenCrest to finalize:
   - Confirm the exact daily windows (start/end in UTC) and the target tokens/sec.
   - Sign an addendum (procurement/commercial) for the week specifying the pin and any credit/overage terms.

I’ve looped in Ben (commercial) to align on commercial changes and Naomi (engineering) to validate feasibility and safe implementation steps. Ben — can you weigh in on the commercial framing (short-term addendum vs. billable burst)? Naomi — can you confirm whether we can do a controlled blackout + soft-reserve without risk to other tenants?

If useful, I can draft the addendum and a short runbook to minimize ops risk. Can we aim to lock this by Nov 10 to give both teams time to test?

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Attachment: SLA_amendment_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 88 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Morales <lena.morales@greencrest.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-05T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Throughput spike & temporary pinning request for BlackWeek

Evelyn / Lena —

Commercially we have two clean levers:

A) Short-term addendum (preferred) — a one-week SLA addendum that specifies guaranteed throughput windows and any pro-rated fee for reserved capacity. Quicker to sign, lower engineering friction.

B) Billable burst credits — keep base contract as-is, charge for overage during the pinned windows at a premium rate. Faster from a contracting perspective but adds billing complexity.

From a GTM perspective, I’d recommend the addendum (A). We can offer a modest usage credit if GreenCrest agrees to a 1-week committed peak (that helps smooth the ask with finance). I’ll draft a clean addendum template and have Legal ready for a quick signature.

Lena — if you can confirm the windows by EOD Nov 8, I’ll circulate the addendum with payment terms and the credit language.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

(Internal note: route the addendum through expedited e-sign with finance approval for credits.)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Morales <lena.morales@greencrest.com>
Date: 2028-11-06T16:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Throughput spike & temporary pinning request for BlackWeek — implementation notes

Evelyn / Ben / Lena —

Technical summary and constraints:

1) Feasibility: We can implement a time-boxed soft-guarantee on your Dedicated pool that acts as a non-preemptible reservation for the specified windows. It’s not a hard physical isolation change — rather a scheduling override that prevents preemption of in-flight requests from your tenancy during the window.

2) Risk & trade-offs:
   - During the pinned windows we will limit opportunistic bursting from other customers on the same infrastructure. This may increase their tail latency slightly but keeps your 99.9th percentile stable.
   - We can’t change the underlying eviction behavior for system-critical maintenance; for that reason Ben’s proposed maintenance blackout is required for any changes to long-running background tasks.

3) Implementation steps (high level):
   - Nov 10: Finalize windows and tokens/sec.
   - Nov 12: Run a synthetic soak test using GreenCrest’s traffic seed on staging. (Lena, we’ll need a 2-hour traffic replay.)
   - Nov 18: Apply runbook to production in a rolling controlled manner and enable blackout during the stated windows Nov 20–27.

4) Observability & rollback:
   - We’ll expose a temporary dashboard (per-route 50/95/99 latency, tokens/sec, queue depth) and an automatic rollback if queue depth exceeds safe thresholds for >5 minutes.

I attached a short runbook that automates the reservation toggle and the rollback hooks. We’ll also create a Jira (INF-4821) to track tasks; linking here.

If everyone signs off on the windows by Nov 10, engineering can be in place for the staging test on Nov 12.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Attachment: runbook_throughput_pinning.md (Markdown, 12 KB)
